open_points.subject: A18/A16 request handling concurrency
open_points.text: State 2 says "no concurrent connections" only in prose, while normative rules define "one process" and "one writer" but do not state whether surface requests are serialized end-to-end.
open_points.question: Can two MCP requests be processed concurrently, and if so what is the required ordering for races like approve vs cancel vs resume on the same run?
options: Strict single-flight request processing (one request at a time globally)
Concurrent request handling allowed, with deterministic per-run conflict resolution
Concurrent handling allowed, last committed store order decides outcomes
open_points.default_guess: Process one request at a time globally to avoid race-dependent behavior.

open_points.subject: A08 rule 7 (accept binding)
open_points.text: "a `proposed` one is read against the manifest as rule 6 does, refused as `binding_stale` when its pin no longer matches, and otherwise becomes `accepted`"
open_points.question: If manifest re-read fails for other rule-6 reasons (missing file, invalid JSON, no instance, no longer invocable), must accept-binding refuse as `binding_stale`, as `manifest_mismatch`, or with distinct reasons?
options: Map every re-read failure at accept time to `binding_stale`
Use distinct refusal codes per failure class
open_points.default_guess: Refuse with `binding_stale` for any accept-time re-read failure, since rule 7 keys acceptance to current pin validity.

open_points.subject: A08 rule 4 idempotency key validation for `read` operations
open_points.text: "for an operation other than `read` each name must equal one input port name of the proposal"
open_points.question: For `read` bindings, may idempotency key fields reference names that are not input ports, and if yes how are those values obtained for key computation/storage?
options: Require key fields to be input ports for all effect classes, including `read`
Allow non-input fields for `read` and ignore key material for reads
Allow non-input fields for `read` and derive from service response/other context
open_points.default_guess: Require key fields to match input ports for all operations.

open_points.subject: A11 attempt numbering vs A13 empty-map record
open_points.text: A11: "An attempt is one execution of a function element, or one send of an operation element... Nothing else takes a number." A13: "A mapped node over an empty list runs nothing... writes one NodeExecution `succeeded` with attempt number 1".
open_points.question: Is the empty-list mapped-node record considered an attempt for numbering semantics, or a non-attempt special record that still carries attempt_number=1?
options: Treat empty-list mapped node as a real attempt #1
Treat it as non-attempt special case with fixed attempt_number=1
Do not emit NodeExecution for empty-list mapped node
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a special non-attempt record that still uses attempt_number=1.

open_points.subject: A16 paging continuation token validation
open_points.text: "The continuation token is the store position of the last item returned; the next page starts below it" with no rule for malformed, future, or missing-position tokens.
open_points.question: What must list operations do when a continuation token is invalid or does not correspond to an existing readable position?
options: Refuse the request as invalid token
Treat it as end-of-list and return empty page
Clamp to nearest lower existing position
open_points.default_guess: Refuse as invalid token to keep paging deterministic and explicit.
